patch.value:
## Why this exists

Pull request 236 ("Keep self-host bundles current in tracker automation", squash commit 1504164) merged while the automated review of its last three commits (b6c7b3b, 1df3b53, bbabb7c: the object-database snapshot reader in `scripts/self-host.ts`) was still running. Those commits were reviewed after the merge. `accept:self-host` and `test/self-host.test.ts` (79 of 79) pass on main for this repository's own content; the findings below are inputs the reader mishandles.

## Findings

Blocking:

1. **`scripts/self-host.ts:756`: lossy path decoding can hide a file from the gate.** Git paths ending in the raw bytes `0x80` and `0x81` both decode to the replacement character; the second entry overwrites the first, and the gate accepted a commit that changed the omitted file. Parse the listing as bytes and reject paths the bundle cannot represent losslessly.
2. **`scripts/self-host.ts:845`: excluded large files exhaust the shared buffer.** Two excluded 33 MiB paths exceeded the 64 MiB buffer and failed both staged writing and verification. Read the configuration first, fetch only the required blobs, and stream their payloads.
3. **`scripts/self-host.ts:807`: the batch parser accepts malformed answers.** Negative or blank sizes, a payload ending in `!` where a newline is required, and trailing output are accepted. Require exactly three header fields, an unsigned safe decimal size, a newline after each payload and exact exhaustion of the stream.
4. **`scripts/self-host.ts:1050`: plain `--write` under `core.autocrlf=true` bundles CRLF files.** After committing the bundle, `--check` rejects it against the LF blobs. Generate the working-tree bundle from Git-cleaned bytes, or refuse converted inputs before writing and direct the caller to `--staged`.

Non-blocking:

5. **`scripts/self-host.ts:770`:** a `160000` entry is rejected even when the configuration explicitly excludes its path. Apply exclusions before rejecting unsupported modes.
6. **`scripts/self-host.ts:1039`:** with a tracked edit staged, `git write-tree` rewrites the caller's index bytes (cache tree). Run against a temporary copy of the index and assert byte equality on the original.
7. **`scripts/self-host.ts:886`:** plain `--write` follows a tracked `self-host.json` symlink, but the staged writer and the gate parse the link target text as JSON and fail. Enforce a regular configuration file consistently, or resolve tracked in-tree targets from the selected snapshot.

## Acceptance

- One regression test per finding that fails on main and passes with the fix; the gate stays fail-closed for every reader error.
- `accept:self-host` passes at the final commit with a regenerated bundle.
- Works on Node 22, Node 26 and Bun as the existing suite does.
Self-host snapshot reader: seven defects found in the post-merge review of the object-database reader

value.text: Continuing the PR 240 follow-up on this branch. The auto re-review left three non-blocking findings on the reader (inherited Git pathspec settings breaking the --literal-pathspecs lookup; the regular-file classification in the working reader re-reading the path after the bytes were captured; the staged writer's scratch index copy dropping a split index's sharedindex base). Verified each finding against the current branch and reproduced the first (Git dies with 'global literal pathspec setting is incompatible' under GIT_GLOB_PATHSPECS/GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS) and the third (git write-tree fails with 'index file open failed' when the shared base sits only beside the selected index) with scratch repositories; closing each class across the package now.

value.author: pi-glm
value.text: Re-review round 2: all three non-blocking findings verified valid and fixed, class-wide. (1) Pathspec isolation (self-host tree lookup): git dies with 'global literal pathspec setting is incompatible with all other global pathspec settings' when a --literal-pathspecs child inherits GIT_GLOB_PATHSPECS or GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS (verified on git 2.53). Rule: a git child whose pathspec semantics the tool pins must not inherit ambient GIT_*_PATHSPECS settings. New isolatedPathspecEnvironment() in git.ts strips the four variables for every runGit child and for the reader's ls-tree spawn; the class instances beyond the finding site are the preflight tracker-cleanliness status (now also pinned with --literal-pathspecs so a tracker path with metacharacters cannot glob-sweep siblings) and the release-changelog-date source inventory, which relies on git's default matching and silently lost every workflow under an ambient GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS. (2) Tied classification (working reader): the rule is that a decision about captured bytes never comes from a second observation of the same path. readSourceFiles now classifies by the leaf type the engine observed when it read (readWorkingFile exposes the pre-read symbolicLink) and refuses any path whose identity changed mid-read; the same split existed in loadConfig (type verdict from one lstat, bytes from a second open) and in writeSnapshot's unchanged check (type from one lstat, bytes from a separate read), both now identity-guarded with the engine's sameFileIdentity; the bundle write itself lands through a same-directory temp + rename so a swapped-in link at the bundle path is replaced, not followed. Engine destruction paths were checked and are already stat-pinned at the action (durability retire/claim refuse destructive_target_changed), so no further instances of the rule are unguarded in the package. (3) Shared index base (staged writer): reproduced that git resolves a split index's base beside the index first with git-dir fallback, and write-tree on a copy without the base fails exactly with 'index file open failed' when the base sits only beside the caller's index; the scratch copy now carries every sharedindex.* sibling, tolerating one garbage-collected between listing and copy.

value.author: pi-glm
value.text: Revert proofs (behavioral revert of each fix in a disposable copy of the sources, tests rerun, fixed sources restored byte-identical and rerun green). Class A: reverting the pathspec isolation and the literal pin made all three regressions fail — the self-host tree-lookup test died with 'git ls-tree failed: fatal: global literal pathspec setting is incompatible with all other global pathspec settings', the preflight tracker-cleanliness test reported the sibling's uncommitted edit as tracker dirt (warn instead of pass), and the release inventory test lost the workflow file entirely; restored, 3/3 pass. Class B: reverting the tied classification and identity guards made all three mid-read replacement regressions fail — the working writer returned the captured CRLF bytes unverified instead of refusing, the configuration loader parsed the captured bytes instead of refusing, and the unchanged check skipped the rewrite leaving a symbolic link at the bundle path; restored, 3/3 pass. Class C: reverting the sharedindex sibling copy failed the staged-writer regression with the finding's exact error, 'fatal: <scratch>/sharedindex.<oid>: index file open failed: No such file or directory'; restored, 1/1 pass.

value.text: The 3694b46 coverage merge exposed a real gap my local sweep could not see (the c8 threshold only runs in CI's merge step): the sharedindex sibling copy's ENOENT-tolerant catch and its non-file filter had no covering tests, leaving the reader file under the 100% per-file threshold. Two adversarial tests close it: one makes a stale base vanish between the directory listing and its copy (the copy must skip it and still write) and plants a directory with the shared-base prefix (skipped unread), the other fails the copy with EACCES and requires the write to fail loudly rather than silently dropping a base. All four verified valid against the code. (1) PRRT_kwDOToJT7M68vvUF: bundle regeneration kept only the group, so a privileged regenerator's own uid became the bundle owner at rename. bundlePermissions now captures uid alongside gid and mode; the temporary is fchowned to the PRESERVED uid and gid before the mode is restored, and the publication-boundary recheck also compares uid, so an ownership change before publication refuses. A refusal to preserve either id propagates and the original bundle stays in place; creation defaults for a new bundle are unchanged. (2) PRRT_kwDOToJT7M68vvUL: writeSnapshot ignored retireNamespace's receipt, so an 'absent' outcome with no move (cleanup race after journal capture) still printed 'wrote'. The receipt is now required to contain a moved entry — which the engine also reports when the destination already holds the requested bytes — otherwise the command fails with a retryable message and the previous bundle is preserved. (3) The heavy-lift companion in the same thread: a crashed bootstrap write leaves a pending publication whose retry let the engine publish the stale candidate behind the retry's own validation and then refuse the now-untracked bundle. writeSnapshot now recovers pending publications explicitly through durability.recoverPublication BEFORE observing/publishing: a recovered candidate equal to the requested bytes reports success (the recovered inode is published, no second candidate is written); a stale recovered candidate may be replaced by the retry (identity-checked allowance), while any other untracked file at the target stays refused. Only a target that was absent before recovery is re-observed, so a present target keeps its single stable observation. (4) PRRT_kwDOToJT7M68vvUN: the POSIX-only filename fixtures (control character, quotes+newline, asterisk) are guarded on win32: the UTF-8 path assertions and the pathspec-environment-key assertions stay on all hosts, the control-character and quoted-path real-file cases skip on win32, and the metacharacter tree-entry lookup constructs its tree directly through git hash-object + update-index --cacheinfo + write-tree so it runs on every host.
